title: Intel Podcast: Scaling Clinical Diagnostic Testing to the Masses
body_text: The rising cost of health care has hit Americans differently depending on their economic status. There is no shortage of news stories covering the reality of those with higher incomes having higher life expectancies than those in lower financial brackets. Healthcare services such as clinical diagnostic testing may be out of reach for those who could really use it. So what are some of the things a company can do to make clinical diagnostic testing more accessible for everyone? How can an important medical test be affordable to all? On this episode of Health & Life Sciences at the Edge, host Michelle Dawn Mooney talks with Intel Head of Business Innovation and Life Science Specialist Blake Harlan and SiPhox Chief Product Officer Mike Dubrovsky about clinical diagnostic testing, the way it is used, and the way its use can be improved. “Clinical diagnostic testing is actually a major part of the [healthcare] system,” says Dubrovsky. “Seventy percent of all medical decisions require diagnostic tests. However, the way that it’s done now is very reactive, so the whole system is based on first the patient having symptoms and then they’re put through a series of tests to try to resolve the problem.” Harlan and Dubrovsky further mention how it’s easy for those in higher income brackets to get tested more often, as those types of tests cost much more than the ones for reactive patients who are presently experiencing symptoms. Read more here and here.

title: Shattering the service quo starts with context
summary: Learn how Atlassian shatters the service quo as a leader in IT service management platforms.
body_text: New industry analyst reports recognize Atlassian as a leader in service management AI is changing expectations for service. Employees want help that feels seamless. Customers want answers without long waits or repeated explanations. Operations teams want to get ahead of incidents and prevent disruptions rather than just respond. Those expectations rest on a critical dependency: context. AI is only useful when it can see the full picture – from people and knowledge to services, assets, and code – and all connections in between. It’s also the place organizations struggle the most. A recent commissioned survey from Forrester Consulting found that only 18% of organizations say their knowledge is part of a broader context graph or unified data layer1. Inability to provide AI systems with sufficient organizational context was cited as the biggest hurdle for enterprises looking to adopt agentic AI in service workflows AND those who had already deployed it. It’s a problem across the entire maturity curve. That is why the latest analyst recognition matters: it validates the shift Atlassian has been building toward, where service teams have the connected context they need to make AI useful across support and operations. Atlassian has been recognized as a Leader in The Forrester Wave™: Conversational AI Platforms for Employee Services, Q3 2026 , with Forrester noting that “Atlassian’s goal with Rovo is to unlock better teamwork using AI. To support this vision, the vendor is prioritizing connected user context across tools, proactive employee support, and embedding Rovo into where people work.” Atlassian has also been recognized as a Leader in the 2026 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for IT Service Management Platforms . The important story is not the recognition alone, though it is certainly appreciated. It is what we believe the research signals: service and operations are moving away from clunky, disconnected experiences toward connected, context-rich ways of working – on and off our platform. Atlassian customers are already sitting on top of one of the richest context layers in the industry. The Teamwork Graph spans over 150 billion objects and relationships – so teams spend less time piecing together answers, while AI has the data it needs to take action. Employee support should meet people where work happens Support teams are often measured on speed, but speed without context creates more friction. Employees don’t want to repeat their request history. Agents don’t want to play detective across a maze of tools. And knowledge – the stuff that makes or breaks good support – is usually scattered across systems, threads, and documents that AI can’t reach. Atlassian’s Service Collection is changing that equation. Rather than bolting AI onto a traditional ticket queue, Atlassian is embedding AI-powered support directly into the collaborative surfaces where work already happens. The Teamwork Graph surfaces trusted knowledge, past requests, relevant people, and connected work across Atlassian and third-party tools, giving AI the depth of context it needs to answer common questions, triage requests, suggest next steps, and connect support teams across the business. Forrester’s report stated the following: Atlassian stands out for its context capabilities (its Teamwork Graph) and ability to embed Rovo into key collaborative surfaces, including multiuser chat channels.” Read the report Employee support does not happen only in a portal. It happens in chat, in search, in Slack channels, and across the teams that own the work. Atlassian’s vision is to proactively bring context to all of those surfaces, improving employee experiences and freeing up service teams to tackle larger, more complex work together. Ops needs context before, during, and after the chaos For operations teams, context is just as critical. During an incident, responders need a clear picture of what changed, who and what is affected, and what has worked before. Without that context, teams lose time switching tools and rebuilding the story from scratch while everyone is asking, “Any update?” We believe Atlassian’s recognition as a Leader in the 2026 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for IT Service Management Platforms underscores the strength of Jira Service Management as a connected service and operations platform. It brings critical service and operations work into one place so teams can move from detection to resolution and learning without losing the plot. AIOps capabilities extend context to help teams spot risks earlier, understand service dependencies, and reduce repeat issues. New integrations bring telemetry, asset intelligence, and log data directly into Jira Service Management, giving teams the diagnostic context they need without constant tool-switching to stop problems in their tracks. The best incident is still the one nobody has to handle at 2 a.m. And when things do inevitably go down, AI and context are key again – from surfacing similar incidents and dependencies, identifying likely root causes, and suggesting mitigation steps. Bye-bye, service quo The future of service is already here, and Atlassian is leading the way. AI-native service management means support and operations teams get the full picture, act with confidence, and stop wasting time piecing together what should have been obvious from the start. Context is what matters. It’s how teams shatter the service quo – one less-frustrating experience at a time. title: Identiv Expands ID-Tiny HF Tag Portfolio to Enable Secure Digital Intelligence for Ultra-Compact Applications
summary: Product family brings one of the industry's broadest selections of ultra-miniaturized HF tags and inlays to healthcare, luxury goods, electronics,…...
body_text: Product family brings one of the industry's broadest selections of ultra-miniaturized HF tags and inlays to healthcare, luxury goods, electronics, and smart packaging markets. SANTA ANA, Calif. , July 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Identiv, Inc. (NASDAQ: INVE), a global leader in RFID- and BLE-enabled Internet of Things (IoT) solutions, today announced the expansion of its ID-Tiny product family, a portfolio of ultra-miniaturized HF/NFC inlays and tags designed to bring secure digital intelligence to compact products, small components, and high-value items where space is extremely limited. The expansion opens new possibilities for connecting physical objects that have historically been too small, too design-sensitive, or too irregularly shaped for conventional RFID and HF/NFC deployments. From jewelry and eyewear to surgical instruments, pharmaceutical vials, wireless earbuds, and personal care product caps, ID-Tiny enables brands and manufacturers to add secure digital functionality without changing how a product looks, feels, or functions. "ID-Tiny is about making digital identity possible in places where it simply wasn't practical before," said Dr. Manfred Mueller, CSO of Identiv. "When you can bring secure, smartphone-readable HF/NFC functionality into form factors no larger than a grain of rice, you unlock entirely new use cases – from verifying a luxury ring's authenticity to tracking the use of a surgical instrument or connecting a patient to dosage instructions from a vial – without compromising performance. That is the power of miniaturization: it makes the smallest physical objects part of the digital world." Unlocking new applications for compact products Across use cases, ID-Tiny helps turn compact products into secure, verifiable touchpoints – enabling authenticity checks, usage tracking, tap-to-pair experiences, patient engagement, and lifecycle visibility in applications where conventional RFID has been difficult to deploy. For luxury goods and fashion brands, ID-Tiny can enable discreet digital certificates of authenticity, Digital Product Passport (DPP) compliance, extended warranty registration, insurance activation, ownership verification, and protection against counterfeiting and gray market diversion. In healthcare, ID-Tiny can support surgical instrument tracking, sterilization cycle monitoring, medical consumable authentication, pharmaceutical vial tracking, and patient-facing digital instructions. In consumer electronics and smart home applications, ID-Tiny can enable product pairing, accessory verification, replacement part authentication, and lifecycle service support. For food, beverage, beauty, and personal care brands, ID-Tiny can help protect product integrity while creating new consumer touchpoints – from authenticity checks and anti-refill protection to usage instructions, loyalty experiences, and post-purchase engagement. This can help organizations reduce counterfeit losses, lower warranty and fraud costs, improve operational efficiency, accelerate authentication processes, improve recall management, and ultimately strengthen consumer trust. Designed for real-world deployment The expanded ID-Tiny portfolio includes eight distinct tags across multiple form factors – one of the industry's broadest selections of miniature HF tags – giving customers flexibility to integrate HF functionality into a wide range of compact products, surfaces, and materials. The family supports ISO15693 and is compatible with leading IC technologies including NXP ICODE® 3 and STMicroelectronics ST25TV, with label sizes smaller than a pencil eraser. Identiv supports customers from design through deployment with encoding and personalization services, application testing, rapid prototyping, and scalable manufacturing capacity. This enables customers to move from concept to production while addressing the RF performance, integration, and manufacturing challenges that come with ultra-miniaturized RFID design. "Smaller tags do more than solve a space problem. They make HF functionality possible in places where there was never room for it before," continued Mueller. "Every connected object starts with a digital identity. By making it practical to add that identity to smaller and often more challenging form factors, ID-Tiny expands what organizations and end users can connect, track, authenticate, and engage with across the physical world." The ID-Tiny product family is available now. For more information about Identiv's ID-Tiny product family or other IoT solutions, please visit Identiv's Product Finder or contact sales@identiv.com . For product imagery, click here . About Identiv Identiv's RFID- and BLE-enabled IoT solutions create digital identities for physical objects, enhancing global connectivity for businesses, people, and the planet. Its solutions, integrated into over 2.0 billion applications worldwide, drive innovation across healthcare, logistics, consumer electronics, luxury goods, smart packaging, and more. Durante siglos, esta comunidad microscópica ha sido aliada de la humanidad, moldeando... The post Explorando el microbioma: la clave para desbloquear el potencial de la salud appeared first on IFF .
body_text: Conclusiones clave El microbioma es un ecosistema vivo que influye silenciosamente en la digestión, la inmunidad e incluso el estado de ánimo. La ciencia moderna apenas está comenzando a comprender la amplitud de su influencia, desde el eje intestino-cerebro hasta la función inmunitaria . La creciente demanda de productos de bienestar con etiquetas limpias ha situado al microbioma en el centro de la innovación. El futuro de la ciencia del microbioma está más allá del horizonte. Apenas estamos comenzando a estudiar cómo las comunidades de microorganismos moldean hoy la digestión, la inmunidad y el estado de ánimo, mientras exploramos lo que podrían hacer posible mañana. Invisible pero indispensable, el microbioma es un ecosistema vivo que influye silenciosamente en la digestión, la inmunidad e incluso el estado de ánimo. Durante siglos, esta comunidad microscópica ha sido aliada de la humanidad, moldeando la salud de maneras que la ciencia moderna apenas comienza a descubrir. Hoy, la creciente demanda de productos enfocados en el bienestar y con etiquetas más limpias ha colocado al microbioma en el centro de la innovación. No somos solo científicos. También somos personas. El camino que va desde la resiliencia microbiana hasta soluciones confiables para la salud del microbioma es importante para nosotros porque nos preocupamos por la salud de nuestros colegas y nuestras familias. Desde el desarrollo pionero de las soluciones probióticas HOWARU® hasta el avance de la investigación sobre microbiomas digestivos, inmunológicos y metabólicos, nuestros científicos combinan ciencia rigurosa, prácticas sostenibles y escala global para ayudar a nuestros socios a crear productos que conecten tanto con el organismo como con el planeta. Exploremos el recorrido del microbioma, desde su papel esencial en la salud humana hasta los beneficios medibles de las soluciones de IFF Health Sciences, incluyendo estudios de caso reales, innovaciones técnicas y la promesa de un futuro guiado por prioridades sostenibles . Comprender el microbioma humano y su impacto en la salud El cuerpo humano alberga billones de microorganismos —bacterias, hongos, arqueas y vírus — conocidos colectivamente como microbioma . Estos organismos aportan más de 150 veces el material genético del genoma humano, ampliando nuestra capacidad de digestión, producción de nutrientes, resiliencia inmunológica e incluso la comunicación con el cerebro. Cuando está equilibrada, esta comunidad genera armonía. Cuando se altera, puede contribuir a enfermedades crónicas como diabetes , obesidad, síndrome de intestino irritable y afecciones cardiovasculares. La ciencia moderna apenas comienza a comprender la amplitud de su influencia, desde la regulación metabólica y la señalización cerebral hasta la función inmunológica. Abordamos el microbioma como ciencia y como historia. Nuestro trabajo en probióticos canaliza décadas de experiencia en biociencias para desarrollar productos que restauran el equilibrio microbiano, aumentan la resiliencia y ayudan a las empresas a responder a la creciente demanda de innovación basada en el microbioma. Explora nuestras soluciones probióticas Explora Beneficios de las soluciones de salud del microbioma de IFF Health Sciences El microbioma es un archivo vivo de hábitos y herencias. Al diseñar para él, honramos tanto la biología como la vida cotidiana. El trabajo de IFF Health Sciences con cepas HOWARU® prioriza la evidencia , seguido de formatos que las personas realmente utilizan. El resultado es un camino claro desde el laboratorio hasta la mesa, donde las soluciones probióticas pueden actuar de manera silenciosa . Salud intestinal y digestiva Ensayos clínicos aleatorizados con probióticos y HOWARU® Restore ( Lactobacillus acidophilus NCFM®, Lactobacillus paracasei Lpc-37™, Bifidobacterium lactis Bi-07™ y Bifidobacterium lactis Bl-04™) han demostrado repetidamente mejoras clínicamente relevantes en la frecuencia de evacuación , la consistencia de las heces , el tiempo de tránsito gastrointestinal y la salud intestinal general . Estos probióticos están disponibles en cápsulas, suplementos dietéticos y alimentos funcionales, lo que permite que los beneficios se integren fácilmente en las rutinas diarias. Soporte inmunológico Estudios con HOWARU® Protect Kids ( Lactobacillus acidophilus NCFM & Bifidobacterium animalis subsp. lactis Bi-07) y Bifidobacterium animalis subsp. lactis Bl-04™ han demostrado que estas cepas ayudan a apoyar la función inmunológica y a reducir la incidencia y duración de síntomas de las vías respiratorias superiores en adultos y niños. Los efectos son específicos de la cepa, dependientes de la dosis y del producto final. Flexibilidad en formulación La robustez de la cepa permite formular productos que no requieren refrigeración. Esa flexibilidad ayuda a la indústria a crear productos únicos y de alta calidad que ofrecen los beneficios para la salud que los consumidores actuales esperan de las soluciones probióticas . Escalabilidad y consistencia Una red global de plantas de fermentación — certificadas en Buenas Prácticas de Fabricación (GMP) y FSSC — respalda un estricto control de especificaciones y un suministro fiable de unidades formadoras de colonias. Esto permite a los equipos realizar lanzamientos a nivel regional y, posteriormente, escalar a escala internacional sin necesidad de reformular las soluciones probióticas clave de IFF Health Sciences . En resumen, esto demuestra cómo las soluciones probióticas trasladan la ciencia del microbioma a aplicaciones cotidianas, preservando al mismo tiempo la viabilidad, la precisión de la dosis y la finalidad de los probióticos destinados a la salud intestinal . Descubra las soluciones probióticas de IFF Health Sciences Descubra Casos de estudio del microbioma en IFF Health Sciences Todo producto parte de una pregunta: ¿Podemos mantener la promesa del microbioma desde el fermentador hasta el momento de su uso sin perder lo esencial? Estas tres instantáneas exploran esa pregunta en la fábrica, la clínica y la vida cotidiana, mostrando cómo la evidencia se une a la práctica en los suplementos moduladores del microbioma, incluidos los probióticos que favorecen la salud intestinal e inmunológica. 1. Mezcla multicepa para el confort digestivo Para evaluar un enfoque basado en múltiples cepas, los investigadores formularon HOWARU® GI Complete — una mezcla de cinco cepas (NCFM®, Lpc-37™, Bi-07™, Bl-04™, HN019™) — y monitorearon los resultados en un estudio clínico de 30 días que incluyó evaluaciones subjetivas. El 85 % de los participantes reportó una mejora en su bienestar gastrointestinal general, así como una reducción de la hinchazón, los gases y las molestias abdominales en general. Estos resultados, basados ​​en los informes de los propios participantes, complementan la literatura científica específica sobre cada cepa y ayudan a comprender cómo pueden actuar los probióticos para la salud intestinal en las rutinas de la vida cotidiana. 2. Cepas probióticas con efectos en el sistema inmunitario en adultos y niños En un estudio clínico de cinco meses en el que se evaluó una formulación orientada a la inmunidad con B. lactis Bl-04™, los adultos experimentaron una reducción del 27 % en el riesgo de infecciones de las vías respiratorias superiores y un retraso en la aparición de los síntomas. En nuestra página de HOWARU® Protect Adult encontrará más detalles e información sobre el formato. Estudiado clínicamente por sus beneficios para la salud respiratoria en adultos, B. lactis Bl-04™, HOWARU® Protect Adult, ayuda a reforzar las defensas inmunitarias naturales del organismo. Por qué es importante: Datos de casos como este ayudan a los formuladores a elegir formatos, establecer rangos operativos y ajustar la dosis en función del rendimiento al final de la vida útil, permitiendo así que las soluciones probióticas de IFF Health Sciences traduzcan la ciencia del microbioma en productos fiables para el uso diario. 3. Resistencia de cepas en productos fermentados En pruebas piloto realizadas en instalaciones de productos lácteos y de origen vegetal, los investigadores realizaron un seguimiento de las cepas antes y después de la liofilización, durante el proceso de mezcla de alto cizallamiento y a lo largo del periodo de almacenamiento hasta el final de su vida útil. La viabilidad se mantuvo en niveles que garantizan la administración de la dosis clínicamente estudiada al finalizar la vida útil del producto, al tiempo que los perfiles sensoriales permanecieron intactos; esto demuestra que dichas soluciones probióticas pueden soportar las tensiones habituales de la fabricación y, simultáneamente, respaldar las declaraciones del etiquetado. Los probióticos garantizan recuentos consistentes de UFC y un desempeño confiable conforme a la declaración de la etiqueta. Eficiencia y ventajas técnicas de nuestras soluciones probióticas La promesa del microbioma comienza como una señal tenue y recorre un largo camino: desde el fermentador y la línea de envasado hasta la mesa del hogar. Para preservar esa señal, diseñamos pensando en los desafíos que las células afrontarán a continuación, no en las condiciones que soportaron ayer. Este enfoque conduce naturalmente a cuatro ejes prácticos que permiten llevar las soluciones probióticas desde la idea inicial hasta su uso cotidiano. 1. Procesamiento diseñado para la estabilidad Desde la fermentación hasta el secado y el envasado final, las operaciones unitarias están ajustadas para limitar el estrés causado por el calor, la humedad y el oxígeno. Las curvas de enfriamiento controladas, los perfiles de liofilización y la mezcla gestionada bajo condiciones de humedad controlada ayudan a preservar los recuentos viables, de modo que las soluciones probióticas de IFF Health Sciences lleguen al mercado con una potencia que se mantiene durante toda la vida útil declarada, sin necesidad de aditivos innecesarios. 2. Supervivencia comprobada de las cepas Antes de la producción a escala, las cepas se evalúan en cuanto a identidad genómica, tolerancia al ácido y a las sales biliares, y estabilidad a largo plazo en matrices relevantes. Los métodos de enumeración y las curvas de degradación orientan la definición de la dosis, de modo que el objetivo de unidades formadoras de colonias (UFC) indicado en la etiqueta se cumpla al final de la vida útil. El objetivo es contar con datos de desempeño transparentes que los equipos técnicos puedan evaluar por sus propios méritos. 3. Aplicaciones versátiles La forma sigue a la función. Las cepas y las matrices se combinan para que los beneficios se mantengan de manera eficaz en formatos como productos lácteos, yogures de origen vegetal, suplementos y bebidas funcionales, todos ellos respaldando la salud intestinal y un microbioma equilibrado sin comprometer la calidad sensorial ni la claridad de la etiqueta. 4. Fabricación confiable y escalable Los sistemas de calidad, la certificación GMP y la transferencia tecnológica reproducible respaldan la consistencia desde las pruebas piloto hasta la producción comercial. Los parámetros documentados para fermentación, mezcla y envasado ayudan a garantizar las UFC declaradas en la etiqueta en diferentes regiones y tamaños de lote a medida que las soluciones probióticas de IFF Health Sciences escalan su producción. Las soluciones probióticas sostenibles de IFF Health Sciences están desarrolladas para respaldar tanto el desempeño del producto como la responsabilidad ambiental. Los principales beneficios en materia de sostenibilidad incluyen: Producción eficiente: Los procesos de fermentación y secado están optimizados para reducir el consumo de energía. Reducción de residuos: Las prácticas de fabricación están diseñadas para minimizar el uso de materias primas y los residuos operativos. Formulaciones compatibles con la etiqueta: Las cepas estables mantienen su viabilidad sin aditivos sintéticos, favoreciendo listas de ingredientes más limpias. Alineación con el consumidor: Ayuda a las marcas a responder a la demanda de productos de bienestar que sean eficaces y ambientalmente responsables. Sostenibilidad en las soluciones para el microbioma El trabajo de cuidar el mundo interior debe respetar también el mundo exterior. A medida que transformamos la ciencia del microbioma en productos para el día a día, diseñamos soluciones con un impacto medible tanto en viabilidad como en huella ambiental. Nuestras soluciones sostenibles de probióticos siguen una idea simple: el desempeño y la responsabilidad avanzan juntos. Producción eficiente Las condiciones de fermentación y secado se ajustan al perfil energético mínimo efectivo y luego se validan frente a los objetivos de estabilidad, de modo que la potencia se preserve mientras se reduce la huella del proceso. Reducción de residuos El uso de materiales se planifica desde la cepa hasta el envase. La optimización de rendimientos, el dimensionamiento adecuado de los lotes y la recuperación de recursos cuando corresponde ayudan a minimizar los insumos y los residuos operativos sin comprometer la calidad. El resultado son declaraciones de ingredientes claras que respetan el formato, la funcionalidad y la intención de las soluciones probióticas . Estas prácticas ayudan a las marcas a cumplir con esa expectativa, conectando un desempeño verificado con un diseño responsable en alimentos funcionales enfocados en el microbioma y probióticos para la salud intestinal . Cada cepa probiótica HOWARU® Premium se somete a pruebas rigurosas mediante el protocolo VERIFY ™ de IFF Health Sciences. Con más de 100 años de experiencia en fermentación y una base de literatura científica publicada que abarca más de 1.200 estudios, desarrollamos soluciones probióticas demostradas para la vida real. Nuestra presencia global en más de 45 países permite lanzamientos regionales y un escalamiento cuidadoso, mientras que la colaboración con instituciones de investigación y expertos clínicos mantiene nuestro trabajo fundamentado en la ciencia. Explore los avances de IFF Health Sciences en el campo del microbioma. Explore El futuro de la investigación del microbioma en IFF Health Sciences El horizonte del microbioma no es una línea de llegada. Es un mapa en constante expansión. Hoy estudiamos cómo las comunidades de microorganismos influyen en la digestión, la inmunidad, el metabolismo y el estado de ánimo, mientras exploramos lo que podrían hacer posible en el futuro. En el Día Mundial del Microbioma , celebramos el esfuerzo compartido que impulsa este avance, desde los datos abiertos hasta el diseño clínico riguroso. Soluciones para la salud del microbioma: Preguntas frecuentes ¿Cómo puedo mantener vivos los probióticos en una bebida? Elija cepas capaces de tolerar la acidez, el frío y el oxígeno, y luego diseñe el proceso de producción en función de ellas. Añada la dosis después de la pasteurización, controle el oxígeno disuelto, establezca temperaturas suaves de mezcla y llenado, y confirme la estabilidad mediante una prueba piloto para garantizar que las UFC prometidas sobrevivan hasta el final de la vida útil. Esto permite que las soluciones probióticas se mantengan alineadas con el propósito de los probióticos para la salud intestinal . ¿Cómo puedo comunicar los beneficios de los probióticos en mi etiqueta? Fundamente cada declaración en una cepa específica respaldada por sólidos datos clínicos en humanos, adapte el lenguaje al marco regulatorio de declaraciones aplicable en su mercado y mantenga claras las especificaciones sobre dosis y duración. Considere la etiqueta como un puente entre la ciencia del microbioma y el uso cotidiano, y no como un simple eslogan. ¿Cómo puedo determinar si mi producto todavía contiene suficientes cultivos vivos? Utilice recuentos en placa para cuantificar las UFC viables y compleméntelos con métodos como qPCR cuando corresponda. Valide el método en la matriz final, supervise la pérdida de viabilidad a lo largo del tiempo y establezca una sobre dosificación que permita alcanzar el recuento declarado al final de la vida útil. Existen programas como VERIFY™ Protocol que ayudan a alinear los métodos analíticos con las UFC declaradas en la etiqueta, de manera que los resultados sean comparables. ¿Por qué elegir cepas de alta calidad y sostenibles durante el desarrollo? Las soluciones probióticas sostenibles y de alta calidad protegen la viabilidad durante el procesamiento y el almacenamiento, reducen la necesidad de aditivos innecesarios y respaldan formulaciones claras y compatibles con la etiqueta. Este enfoque disminuye el riesgo de reformulación y ayuda a que los productos mantengan los beneficios previstos desde la etapa piloto hasta la producción a escala. ¿Tiene más preguntas sobre soluciones para el microbioma? CONTÁCTENOS La información presentada aquí tiene fines exclusivamente informativos sobre probióticos. Ninguna de las sustancias mencionadas debe considerarse destinada al tratamiento, cura o prevención de ninguna enfermedad. Las aprobaciones regulatorias, las condiciones de uso y las declaraciones autorizadas varían entre distintas jurisdicciones y deben evaluarse de acuerdo con la normativa vigente en cada país. The post Explorando el microbioma: la clave para desbloquear el potencial de la salud appeared first on IFF .

title: Stryker releases 2024 Comprehensive Report, highlighting a year of innovation, impact and growth
summary: Stryker is pleased to announce the publication of our 2024 Comprehensive Report, showcasing another year of strong financial performance, innovation, and progress toward our corporate and sustainability commitments.
body_text: Stryker is pleased to announce the publication of our 2024 Comprehensive Report, showcasing another year of strong financial performance, innovation and progress toward our corporate and sustainability commitments. This year’s report highlights how we are driving meaningful change for patients, customers, employees and communities worldwide. From launching transformative medical technologies to expanding access to care, Stryker remains focused on making healthcare better. “Our strategy is working,” says Lobo. “We continue to drive strong growth and performance across our key metrics. I believe Stryker’s best days are ahead of us.”

title: Agent Credentials vs. Human Credentials
summary: Agentic Fabriq is the identity and permissioning layer for AI agents. Per-agent identity, least-privilege access, full audit logs, and one-click revocation across MCP, OAuth, and agent frameworks. Drop-in with Okta, Azure AD, and Google Workspace.
body_text: Overview An AI agent should not be treated exactly like a human user. But it should not be treated like an invisible background script either. It sits somewhere in between — an autonomous actor that takes real actions against real systems, on its own initiative or on behalf of someone else. Nowhere does this in-between status matter more than with credentials . The keys, tokens, and accounts an agent uses to reach enterprise systems determine what it can touch, what gets recorded when it acts, and whether anyone can answer the question that always comes later: who did this, and were they allowed to? The fastest way to get an agent working is to hand it a human's credential or a shared service account. It is also the fastest way to lose the ability to govern it. This post explains why agent credentials and human credentials are fundamentally different, and what a healthier model looks like. Two Kinds of Credentials Human credentials are tied to people. They live inside an identity stack that has matured over decades — login systems, single sign-on, multi-factor authentication, device posture checks, conditional access, and user access policies. All of these assume there is a person on the other end who can be challenged, verified, and held accountable. Agent credentials are tied to non-human actors. In practice they take the form of API keys, OAuth tokens, service accounts, or delegated credentials that let an agent authenticate to enterprise systems and act. None of the human assumptions hold. There is no one to prompt for MFA, no device to inspect, no person whose behavior the access policy was written around. The mistake is reusing the human toolkit for the non-human case. A credential built to represent a person, governed by controls designed for people, cannot cleanly represent an agent. The difference is not cosmetic — it changes what your audit trail can prove and what your access controls can enforce. The Borrowed-Access Problem When an agent uses a human's credential directly, the agent inherits everything that person can do — and every action it takes is recorded as if the person performed it. Consider a financial close assistant that runs under a controller's account because that was the simplest way to give it access to the general ledger. The agent can now post journal entries, reclassify accounts, and pull bank reconciliation data — the full surface of a senior finance role. When the entries it posts are reviewed three weeks later, the ledger shows the controller made them. There is no way, from the records alone, to tell which entries were human judgment and which were the agent acting on a rule it inferred. This creates two problems at once: It weakens auditability. You cannot separate what the human did from what the agent did, because both wear the same identity. It expands risk. The agent can perform everything the user can perform, including actions far outside the narrow task it was built for. Borrowed access feels like delegation, but it is really impersonation. The system cannot tell the difference, which means your controls cannot either. The Shared-Account Problem The other common shortcut is the opposite of borrowing a person's identity: giving many agents one shared service account. This is appealing because a single set of keys is easy to provision and rotate, and it sidesteps the question of agent identity entirely. Imagine a data platform where a half-dozen analytics agents — one summarizing pipeline health, one refreshing dashboards, one flagging anomalies, one backfilling tables — all authenticate to the warehouse with the same service account. One night, a destructive query truncates a production table. The warehouse logs show the action came from svc-analytics . Which agent issued it? Nobody can say. The shared account that made provisioning easy has made attribution impossible. Shared credentials collapse many distinct actors into one. The moment you need to attribute an action, scope a blast radius, or revoke one misbehaving agent without breaking the others, the shared account becomes the thing standing in your way. Distinct Identity, Preserved Context A better model gives each agent its own distinct identity and credentials, while still preserving the human context when an agent acts on someone's behalf. These two ideas work together rather than against each other. The agent has an identity of its own, so its actions are never mistaken for a person's. But when it acts for a user — pulling a record that user is entitled to see, or submitting a request the user initiated — that user context travels with the action. The result is an audit trail that can express the full picture: A specific agent performed a specific action for a specific user, under a specific permission policy, at a specific time. For example, an HR onboarding agent provisioning a new hire's accounts should show in the record as the onboarding agent , acting on behalf of the HR coordinator who triggered the request, exercising a provisioning permission scoped to onboarding. None of that detail survives if the agent simply logs in as the coordinator. All of it survives when identity and context are kept separate but linked. This is what gives an enterprise both traceability — the ability to reconstruct who did what — and control — the ability to allow or deny based on the real actor. Scoping Agents Differently Agent credentials should also be scoped on a different basis than human credentials. A person typically holds broad access because of their job role — a procurement manager can view every supplier contract, raise purchase orders, and approve invoices below a threshold, because the role demands range and judgment across many situations. An agent has no comparable need for breadth. It exists to perform a specific workflow, so its credential should grant only the access that workflow requires — nothing more. A procurement intake agent that drafts purchase orders from approved requisitions does not need to read every contract in the repository or approve invoices. It needs to read the requisition, look up the relevant vendor, and create a draft order for a human to approve. Scoping its credential to exactly that surface means a prompt injection or a logic error cannot escalate into approving payments — because the credential never carried that power in the first place. Human scope follows the role. It is broad by design, because people handle exceptions and edge cases. Agent scope follows the workflow. It is narrow by design, because the agent does one defined job. Applying a human-shaped role to an agent gives it far more reach than its task justifies. Scoping to the workflow keeps the credential's power proportional to the work. A Different Lifecycle Agent credentials also need different lifecycle controls, and this is where reused human credentials quietly become a liability. When an employee leaves, their access is offboarded through familiar machinery — HR records a termination, the identity system disables the account, downstream entitlements fall away. The trigger is a person walking out the door, and the process is well rehearsed. When an agent is retired, no person is leaving the company. A security log-triage agent that gets replaced by a newer version does not generate an HR event. Its keys do not expire on their own. If the credential was its own managed object, it can be explicitly revoked when the agent is decommissioned. If it was a borrowed human login or a shared service account, there is often nothing that clearly says this access existed only for that agent and can now be removed — so it lingers, an unowned set of keys with real reach into your systems. An agent credential needs its own birth and its own death. Provisioned when the agent is registered, revoked when the agent is retired — independent of any human's lifecycle, because the agent has a lifecycle of its own. In Practice Translating the principle into operational terms, an agent credential carries a few traits that a borrowed or shared one cannot: • Unique to the agent. One credential maps to one agent, so every action is attributable to a single actor. • Scoped to the workflow. Permissions match what the task needs, not what a comparable human role would hold. • Context-aware. When acting for a user, the user's identity rides alongside the agent's, so the record shows both. • Independently revocable. The credential can be killed when the agent retires, without touching any person's access. Concretely, the gap shows up in the audit record. Compare what each model can prove about the same warehouse query: # Shared service account — attribution lost actor: svc-analytics action: DELETE FROM prod.orders WHERE ... on_behalf_of: (unknown) permission: (account-level, unscoped) # Distinct agent identity — attribution preserved actor: agent:anomaly-detector-v3 action: DELETE FROM prod.orders WHERE ... on_behalf_of: user:dpatel@enterprise (data-eng) permission: analytics.read-only # <- denied: write not in scope result: blocked The same scoping that makes the action attributable also makes it preventable. With a workflow-scoped, read-only credential, the destructive query never executes — and if it had, the record would name the agent, the user behind it, and the policy that should have applied. The Principle: Separation The thread running through all of this is separation . Agent identity should be separate from human identity. Agent scope should be separate from human scope. Agent lifecycle should be separate from human lifecycle. In plain terms: agents should not silently borrow human access, and they should not hide behind shared credentials. They should have managed, scoped, and auditable credentials of their own — provisioned deliberately, scoped to the task, and revoked when the agent's job is done. An agent with its own credential is an actor you can see, scope, and stop. That is what makes agent activity governable — not a claim that the agent is safe, but a record that proves what it did and the boundaries it worked within.

title: Black On The Square
summary: Mayor of London’s Black On The Square festival returns to celebrate Black communities and culture
body_text: Mayor of London’s Black On The Square festival returns to celebrate Black communities and culture Celebrate Black culture and creativity at Black On The Square on Saturday 7 September. From 12-6pm, enjoy free performances with music, dance, and spoken word, plus food, fashion, film, art, and more. The stage line-up will be headlined by award-winning actor and rapper Bashy. Performers will also include Kofi Stone, Afrobeat DJ collective Cultur FM, hip hop star Phoebs, Afro-electronic DJ and singer Karen Nyame KG, and Krar Collective. From London, via Addis Ababa, this trio’s unique and powerful take on Ethiopian music has made them rising stars in world music. Lewisham’s finest, Shingai of Noisettes fame, will be performing too. Expect her to live up to her name, which means ‘be bold’ in the Shona language! There’s plenty to keep the kids entertained with special activities hosted by Culture Tree and face painting with NyGlorious Face Arts. Elsewhere, the brilliant bustling market promises a feast for all the senses. Sample delights from Mauritius, Guyana, Jamaica, Nigeria, Ghana, and beyond – from plantain bites to fusion fish and chips and delicious vegan ice cream. You’ll find stalls selling everything from coats and bags to headwear, home décor, candles, art prints, jewellery, and books too. There are also workshops to join, with a strong focus on the growing Black business community. Get a free business MOT from Foundervine, SME support and advice for creatives from My Runway Group. And if fabric is more your style, don’t miss Fée Uhssi’s colour therapy and tote bag workshop. Returning for a second year, this free event in Trafalgar Square is brought to you by Mayor of London, Sadiq Khan. Find out more: www.london.gov.uk/black-on-the-square

title: The Engineering Bug: A Founding Developer Passes the Torch
summary: This summer, our most senior engineer brought his son onto the Hadrius team for an internship — and a taste of what industry is all about.
body_text: In January 2024, engineer Daniel Van Tassell — DVT to everyone here — became Hadrius' first non-founder employee. This summer, he brought in one of the newest members of our team: his son Jack , 14, who wraps up a two-month internship today before starting 9th grade in the fall. Thousands of miles removed from their Utah home, Jack has spent his summer at Hadrius working under the close supervision of his father and becoming a regular part of the dev team: shipping code, filling tickets, and even building a flagship archiving integration. Along the way, DVT has watched with pride as his son put to use the engineering skills he began inculcating while Jack was still in the crib — exceeding every expectation along the way. We sat down with them to talk about how a teenager gets prepared to earn a spot on a real, fast-moving dev team. ‍ Jack and Daniel Van Tassell at the Hadrius office, July 2026 ‍ Q: How does a 14-year-old end up interning at a compliance software company? DVT: It started years ago. Six years old was "here's your own machine, learn to type, build your own computer." Seven, he started modding his own Minecraft server. Eight, he started Python. From there it was just one hour a day, four days a week: let's build a little widget, let's make a website, let's take a class, let's make a mobile app. Little steps, walking forward, for years. My opinion is that kids can do a lot more than we give them access to. They have the same logic adults have. If you push, they respond. ‍ Q: Was there a specific moment you thought, "he's ready for a real job"? DVT: Last fall. We were doing our own projects at home — databases, migrations, working through problems — and I kept noticing that the stuff we were doing after school was comparable to tickets the team around me was solving. At some point you hit the thing you can't teach at home, which is that you're rarely ever a solo developer. The real level-up is learning to work with other people. So I went to [co-founder & CTO] Allen and asked, "How would you feel about a 14-year-old intern?" A few months later, Jack and I moved to Brooklyn for the summer. ‍ Jack has attended two PyCons with his father. ‍ Q: Jack, what's your version of how you got into this? Jack: I've always loved technology, and I've always liked building things and solving problems. You combine those two and you basically get coding. You build something to solve someone else's problem. Construction is the physical version of that; coding is the technological version. These days I pick most of my own projects. It's not just what he thinks I should do anymore — I have enough experience to actually weigh the pros and cons and decide what I want to work on. ‍ Q: This summer was the first time you really started using AI as a coding tool. What's been your takeaway? Jack: I wasn't allowed to lean on it much at home, so this was the first time I used it seriously — and learning it was one of my goals, because it's not going away. But it's not as simple as clicking yes, yes, yes. If you just approve everything the model wants to do, you're handing over control, and it's almost never fully right. It gets progressively worse, and once it goes bad, you can't fix it, because you don't know what's happening anymore. You have to actually understand what you're building. DVT: AI's great when you have a plan and you're checking in frequently. The risk is losing the mental model. As long as you keep that, it's just another upgrade in the toolchain, like going from a hammer to a drill press to a CNC machine. The craft underneath doesn't change. Daniel and Jack Van Tassell (aged 10) in 2022 ‍ Q: DVT, how much of the summer was you looking over his shoulder? DVT: At the start, a lot. The planning phase was probably 80% me: "Here's the task; what's your plan? "If you're stuck for more than half an hour, come find me — but first, what did you try, what did you look up, what did the tools suggest, where exactly are you stuck?" By the end, it flipped. I gave him a ticket, checked in the next day, and asked what his plan was. He said, "It's done. The PR's up." He'd found the problem, written tests, and put it up for review already. That's the difference between a junior and continuing to learn: the tests, the verification, the changing direction well. If he couldn't take feedback, this summer wouldn't have worked at all. ‍ Four years later. ‍ Q: What are each of you most proud of? Jack: I don't know how high the expectations were for a 14-year-old, but getting past anyone's bar is hard, and I think I did. It's different from something like speaking up at a Python convention as a kid — here, it's a workplace. They expect you to actually work. DVT: Watching someone grow into their own and fully believe they belong. Everyone carries impostor syndrome. Watching him break through that happened in front of me this summer. That's a proud-dad moment. And then getting out of the way. It's not about me. ‍ Q: Jack, do you want to come back? Jack: Oh, yeah. DVT: That's the next conversation: Him making the case himself. “This is what I built, this is what I shipped, and I'd like to return.” Which is exactly the right way to do it. Jack's third goal for the summer, after ‘learn to use AI’ and ‘learn to work on a team,’ was simply: come back. Two down. We'll see about the third. ‍ If you'd like to join a team of builders and owners, we're hiring: hadrius.com/careers

title: CAPTCHA and blocker handling: keeping browser agents recoverable
summary: How Ramain combines managed browser capabilities, OTP polling, human handoff, and recovery states when a portal blocks automation.
body_text: [Recovery and escalation] Portal blockers are not one problem. They include CAPTCHA, MFA, OTP codes, popups, human review points, and ambiguous browser states. Ramain handles them as recoverable workflow events rather than treating every blocker as a failed automation. The first layer is the browser provider Managed cloud browsers can be launched with CAPTCHA-solving capabilities. This handles common page-level challenges before the workflow has to escalate. If the portal requires user-specific input, the workflow system has explicit capabilities for OTP polling, human-in-the-loop browser handoff, and agent prompts. Escalation is part of the graph The workflow editor includes block capabilities for OTP and human review. An Email Poll Agent can retrieve emailed codes, while a Human Review Agent can pause and ask a person to operate or confirm the live browser. That means blockers are modeled as durable workflow nodes instead of being buried inside brittle exception handling. What gets logged Run statuses distinguish waiting, recovering, fallback, completed, recovered, failed, and terminated states. OTP progress and review decisions are carried into the UI so the operator can see why a run paused. The goal is not to pretend every portal can be fully automated. The goal is to keep the workflow honest and recoverable. Key takeaway Ramain treats blockers as workflow states. Some can be handled automatically, and the rest can pause for the right human or OTP input without losing the run.
